title.zh: 卷二十五 志第一 天文一
title.raw: 卷二十五 志第一 天文一 Volume 25 Treatises 1: Astronomy 1

sentences.zh: 天文一

translations.literal: Astronomy 1.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on Astronomy, Part One.

sentences.zh: 自司馬遷述《天官》，而歷代作史者皆志天文。

translations.literal: From Sima Qian's exposition of the 'Heavenly Offices,' historians of every dynasty have recorded astronomy in their treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Sima Qian set forth the 'Heavenly Offices' in the Records, successive dynastic histories have included a treatise on astronomy.

sentences.zh: 惟《遼史》獨否，謂天象昭垂，千古如一，日食、天變既著本紀，則天文志近於衍。

translations.literal: Only the History of Liao alone refused, saying celestial signs are displayed and hang down, the same through a thousand ages; eclipses and heavenly changes are already set forth in the basic annals, so an astronomy treatise is nearly superfluous.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Liao alone demurred, arguing that the heavens display the same omens age after age and that, since solar eclipses and celestial anomalies already appear in the annals, a separate astronomy treatise verged on redundancy.

sentences.zh: 其說頗當。

translations.literal: Its statement is quite fitting.
translations.idiomatic: That objection has considerable force.

sentences.zh: 夫《周髀》、《宣夜》之書，安天、窮天、昕天之論，以及星官占驗之說，晉史已詳，又見《隋志》，謂非衍可乎。

translations.literal: Now the books Zhou Bi and Xuan Ye, the discussions of stabilizing heaven, exhausting heaven, and discerning heaven, and moreover the theories of star-offices and prognostication—already detailed in the Jin history and again seen in the Sui Treatises—can one call these not superfluous?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Zhou Bi and Xuan Ye texts, debates over whether heaven is at rest or exhaustible, methods of inspecting the sky, and the whole literature of star-offices and omen verification were already treated at length in the Jin History and repeated in the Sui bibliographic monographs—are those to be dismissed as mere padding?

sentences.zh: 論者謂天文志首推晉、隋，尚有此病，其他可知矣。

translations.literal: Discussants say astronomy treatises are ranked first in Jin and Sui, yet still have this fault; the rest may be known.
translations.idiomatic: Critics observe that even the astronomy treatises of the Jin and Sui histories—often held up as the best—suffer this flaw; lesser compilations need hardly be mentioned.

sentences.zh: 然因此遂廢天文不志，亦非也。

translations.literal: Yet because of this to abolish astronomy and not record it is also not right.
translations.idiomatic: Still, to abandon the astronomy treatise altogether on that account would itself be mistaken.

sentences.zh: 天象雖無古今之異，而談天之家，測天之器，往往後勝於前。

translations.literal: Celestial signs though without ancient and modern difference, yet those who discourse on heaven and instruments that measure heaven often excel later over earlier.
translations.idiomatic: The visible heavens may not change from age to age, but theories of the cosmos and the instruments used to measure it frequently improve with time.

sentences.zh: 無以志之，使一代製作之義泯焉無傳，是亦史法之缺漏也。

translations.literal: Without recording them, to let one generation's productions and meanings perish without transmission is also a gap in historiographic method.
translations.idiomatic: If nothing is recorded, an entire generation's observational and computational achievements may vanish without trace—a real breach of historiographic duty.

sentences.zh: 至於彗孛飛流，暈適背抱，天之所以示儆戒者，本紀中不可盡載，安得不別志之。

translations.literal: As for comets and broom-stars, flying streams, halos, occultations, and opposed embraces—what heaven uses to show warning—the basic annals cannot fully carry them; how can one not separately record them?
translations.idiomatic: Comets, meteors, halos, occultations, and mutual embraces—the heavens' warnings—cannot all be crowded into the annals; they must have a separate treatise.

sentences.zh: 明神宗時，西洋人利瑪竇等入中國，精於天文、歷算之學，發微闡奧，運算制器，前此未嘗有也。

translations.literal: In the time of the Ming Shenzong, Westerners Matteo Ricci and others entered China, skilled in astronomy and calendrical calculation, revealing the subtle and expounding the abstruse, operating calculations and making instruments—never before had there been such.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wanli emperor, Western scholars such as Matteo Ricci arrived in China versed in astronomy and calendrics, opening subtle doctrines, explaining recondite principles, and devising computational methods and instruments unlike anything known before.

sentences.zh: 茲掇其要，論著於篇。

translations.literal: Here their essentials are gathered and discussed and set forth in the chapter.
translations.idiomatic: What follows selects their chief points and sets them out in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 而《實錄》所載天象星變殆不勝書，擇其尤異者存之。

translations.literal: But the Veritable Records' carried celestial signs and star changes nearly cannot all be written; the especially strange are chosen and preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Records alone contain more celestial and stellar anomalies than could be listed; only the most remarkable are retained here.

sentences.zh: 日食備載本紀，故不復書。

translations.literal: Solar eclipses are fully recorded in the basic annals, therefore they are not written again.
translations.idiomatic: Solar eclipses already appear in full in the annals and are not repeated here.

sentences.zh: ▲兩儀 《楚詞》言「圜則九重，孰營度之」，渾天家言「天包地如卵裡黃」，則天有九重，地為渾圓，古人已言之矣。

translations.literal: ▲ Two Instruments The Songs of Chu say 'Round, then ninefold—who planned and measured it?'; armillary-sphere masters say 'Heaven wraps earth like yolk in an egg'—then heaven has nine layers and earth is a perfect sphere; the ancients already spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Heaven and Earth The Songs of Chu ask, 'Round and ninefold—who measured it?' Armillary cosmologists said, 'Heaven enfolds the earth as the yolk lies in an egg'—nine celestial tiers and a spherical earth were already ancient ideas.

sentences.zh: 西洋之說，既不背於古，而有驗於天，故表出之。

translations.literal: The Western teaching, neither contrary to antiquity and yet verified against heaven, therefore is tabulated and brought forth.
translations.idiomatic: The Western account neither contradicts the ancients nor fails when tested against the sky; it is therefore set forth here.

sentences.zh: 其言九重天也，曰最上為宗動天，無星辰，每日帶各重天，自東而西左旋一周，次曰列宿天，次曰填星天，次曰歲星天，次曰熒惑天，次曰太陽天，次曰金星天，次曰水星天，最下曰太陰天。

translations.literal: Its speaking of ninefold heaven says: highest is the Primum Mobile heaven, without stars; daily it carries each layered heaven from east to west in one leftward revolution; next is the Lodge heaven, next Saturn heaven, next Jupiter heaven, next Mars heaven, next Sun heaven, next Venus heaven, next Mercury heaven; lowest is the Moon heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On the nine celestial spheres: the highest is the primum mobile, bearing no stars; each day it drags every lower sphere in one westward (apparent) rotation; below it lie, in order, the sphere of fixed stars (xiu), Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and at the bottom the Moon.

sentences.zh: 自恆星天以下八重天，皆隨宗動天左旋。

translations.literal: From the Fixed-Star heaven downward the eight layered heavens all follow the Primum Mobile in leftward rotation.
translations.idiomatic: All eight spheres below the primum mobile—including the sphere of fixed stars—share its daily westward motion.

sentences.zh: 然各天皆有右旋之度，自西而東，與蟻行磨上之喻相符。

translations.literal: Yet each heaven all has a rightward-revolution degree, from west to east, matching the simile of an ant walking on a millstone.
translations.idiomatic: Each sphere also has its own eastward (prograde) motion, west to east—the familiar image of an ant crawling on a turning millstone.

sentences.zh: 其右旋之度，雖與古有增減，然無大異。

translations.literal: Its rightward-revolution degrees, though with increase and decrease compared to antiquity, yet without great difference.
translations.idiomatic: Those prograde rates differ slightly from ancient figures but not materially.

sentences.zh: 惟恆星之行，即古歲差之度。

translations.literal: Only the motion of fixed stars is the ancient precession degree.
translations.idiomatic: The apparent drift of the fixed stars is precisely what the ancients called precession.

sentences.zh: 古謂恆星千古不移，而黃道之節氣每歲西退。

translations.literal: Antiquity said fixed stars through a thousand ages do not move, yet the ecliptic's solar terms each year retreat westward.
translations.idiomatic: Older Chinese astronomy held the fixed stars eternally unmoved while the solar terms along the ecliptic slipped westward year by year.

sentences.zh: 彼則謂黃道終古不動，而恆星每歲東行。

translations.literal: They then say the ecliptic through the ages does not move, while fixed stars each year go eastward.
translations.idiomatic: The Western school holds the ecliptic fixed and the fixed stars advancing eastward annually.

sentences.zh: 由今考之，恆星實有動移，其說不謬。

translations.literal: Examined from today, fixed stars truly have motion and shift; their doctrine is not wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Modern observation confirms that the fixed stars do shift; the Western account is sound.

sentences.zh: 至於分周天為三百六十度，命日為九十六刻，使每時得八刻無奇零，以之布算制器，甚便也。

translations.literal: As for dividing the full circuit of heaven into three hundred sixty degrees and ordering the day as ninety-six quarter-hours, making each double-hour obtain eight quarter-hours without odd remainder, using this to lay out calculation and make instruments—very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: They also divide the celestial circle into 360 degrees and the day into 96 ke (quarter-hours), so each of the twelve double-hours contains exactly eight ke without fractional scraps—a great convenience for calculation and instrument design.

sentences.zh: 其言地圓也，曰地居天中，其體渾圓，與天度相應。

translations.literal: Its speaking of earth as round says: earth dwells in heaven's center, its body a perfect sphere, corresponding to celestial degrees.
translations.idiomatic: On the earth's form: it rests at the center of the heavens, a sphere whose dimensions match celestial degrees.

sentences.zh: 中國當赤道之北，故北極常現，南極常隱。

translations.literal: China lies north of the equator, therefore the north pole is always visible and the south pole always hidden.
translations.idiomatic: China stands north of the equator, so the north celestial pole is always above the horizon and the south pole always below.

sentences.zh: 南行二百五十里則北極低一度，北行二百五十里則北極高一度。

translations.literal: Traveling south two hundred fifty li then the north pole lowers one degree; traveling north two hundred fifty li then the north pole rises one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Travel two hundred fifty li south and the north pole sinks one degree; travel two hundred fifty li north and it rises one degree.

sentences.zh: 東西亦然。

translations.literal: East and west are likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same principle governs east–west motion.

sentences.zh: 亦二百五十里差一度也。

translations.literal: Also two hundred fifty li differs by one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Again, one degree corresponds to two hundred fifty li on the ground.

sentences.zh: 以周天度計之，知地之全周為九萬里也。

translations.literal: Calculating by degrees of the full circuit of heaven, one knows the earth's full circumference is ninety thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: From the 360 degrees of the celestial circle one derives the earth's full circumference: ninety thousand li.

sentences.zh: 以周徑密率求之，得地之全徑為二萬八千六百四十七里又九分裡之八也。

translations.literal: Seeking by circumference–diameter ratio one obtains the earth's full diameter as twenty-eight thousand six hundred forty-seven li and eight-ninths of a li.
translations.idiomatic: Applying the precise ratio of circumference to diameter yields a terrestrial diameter of 28,647 li and eight-ninths of a li.

sentences.zh: 又以南北緯度定天下之縱。

translations.literal: Again by north–south latitude one fixes the realm's north–south extent.
translations.idiomatic: North–south latitude fixes the north–south span of the world.

sentences.zh: 凡北極出地之度同，則四時寒暑靡不同。

translations.literal: Wherever the degree of the north pole above the ground is the same, the four seasons' cold and heat are without difference.
translations.idiomatic: Places sharing the same polar altitude experience the same seasons and climate.

sentences.zh: 若南極出地之度與北極出地之度同，則其晝夜永短靡不同。

translations.literal: If the degree of the south pole above the ground equals the degree of the north pole above the ground, then their day–night length and brevity are without difference.
translations.idiomatic: Where the south pole rises as far above the horizon as the north pole does in the northern hemisphere, day and night lengths match those latitudes in the north.

sentences.zh: 惟時令相反，此之春，彼為秋，此之夏，彼為冬耳。

translations.literal: Only the seasons are opposite: here spring, there autumn; here summer, there winter.
translations.idiomatic: Only the seasons are reversed—spring here is autumn there, summer here winter there.

sentences.zh: 以東西經度定天下之衡，兩地經度相去三十度，則時刻差一辰。

translations.literal: By east–west longitude one fixes the realm's east–west extent; two places whose longitudes differ by thirty degrees differ in time by one double-hour.
translations.idiomatic: East–west longitude fixes the world's lateral extent: a difference of thirty degrees in longitude equals one double-hour (chen) in local time.

sentences.zh: 若相距一百八十度，則晝夜相反焉。

translations.literal: If separated by one hundred eighty degrees, then day and night are opposite.
translations.idiomatic: At one hundred eighty degrees apart, day and night are reversed.

sentences.zh: 其說與《元史》札馬魯丁地圓之旨略同。

translations.literal: Its doctrine and the History of Yuan's Jamal al-Din on the round earth share the same purport in brief.
translations.idiomatic: This doctrine broadly agrees with Jamal al-Din's spherical-earth theory recorded in the History of Yuan.

sentences.zh: ▲七政 日月五星各有一重天，其天皆不與地同心，故其距地有高卑之不同。

translations.literal: ▲ Seven Luminaries Sun, moon, and five stars each have one layered heaven; their heavens all are not concentric with earth, therefore their distance from earth has high and low difference.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ The Seven Luminaries The sun, moon, and five planets each occupy its own sphere; none is centered on the earth, so their distances vary.

sentences.zh: 其最高最卑之數，皆以地半徑准之。

translations.literal: Their highest and lowest numbers all take the earth's semi-diameter as standard.
translations.idiomatic: Maximum and minimum distances are all expressed in units of the earth's radius.

sentences.zh: 太陽最高距地為地半徑者一千一百八十二，最卑一千一百零二。

translations.literal: The sun's highest distance from earth is one thousand one hundred eighty-two earth semi-diameters; lowest one thousand one hundred two.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's greatest distance is 1,182 earth radii, its least 1,102.

sentences.zh: 太陰最高五十八，最卑五十二。

translations.literal: The moon's highest fifty-eight; lowest fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: The moon's greatest distance is 58 earth radii, its least 52.

sentences.zh: 填星最高一萬二千九百三十二，最卑九千一百七十五。

translations.literal: Saturn's highest twelve thousand nine hundred thirty-two; lowest nine thousand one hundred seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn's greatest distance is 12,932 earth radii, its least 9,175.

sentences.zh: 歲星最高六千一百九十，最卑五千九百一十九。

translations.literal: Jupiter's highest six thousand one hundred ninety; lowest five thousand nine hundred nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter's greatest distance is 6,190 earth radii, its least 5,919.

sentences.zh: 熒惑最高二千九百九十八，最卑二百二十二。

translations.literal: Mars's highest two thousand nine hundred ninety-eight; lowest two hundred twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Mars's greatest distance is 2,998 earth radii, its least 222.

sentences.zh: 太白最高一千九百八十五，最卑三百。

translations.literal: Venus's highest one thousand nine hundred eighty-five; lowest three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Venus's greatest distance is 1,985 earth radii, its least 300.

sentences.zh: 辰星最高一千六百五十九，最卑六百二十五。

translations.literal: Mercury's highest one thousand six hundred fifty-nine; lowest six hundred twenty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury's greatest distance is 1,659 earth radii, its least 625.

sentences.zh: 若欲得七政去地之裡數，則以地半徑一萬二千三百二十四里通之。

translations.literal: If one wishes to obtain the seven luminaries' li-distance from earth, then multiply through with the earth semi-diameter of twelve thousand three hundred twenty-four li.
translations.idiomatic: To convert these figures into li from the earth's surface, multiply by the terrestrial radius of 12,324 li.

sentences.zh: 又謂填星形如瓜，兩側有兩小星如耳。

translations.literal: Again they say Saturn's form is like a melon; on two sides two small stars like ears.
translations.idiomatic: They also report Saturn shaped like a gourd, flanked by two small stars like ears.

sentences.zh: 歲星四周有四小星，繞行甚疾。

translations.literal: Jupiter on four sides has four small stars, revolving very swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Four small stars circle Jupiter rapidly on all sides.

sentences.zh: 太白光有盈缺，如月之弦望。

translations.literal: Venus's light has waxing and waning, like the moon's crescent and full.
translations.idiomatic: Venus shows phases like the moon—from thin crescent to full disk.

sentences.zh: 用窺遠鏡視之，皆可悉睹也。

translations.literal: Using the far-sight tube to view them, all can be fully seen.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed through the telescope, all these features can be seen clearly.

sentences.zh: 余詳《歷志》。

translations.literal: The rest are detailed in the Treatise on the Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Further particulars appear in the Treatise on the Calendar.

sentences.zh: ▲恆星 崇禎初，禮部尚書徐光啟督修曆法，上《見界總星圖》。

translations.literal: ▲ Fixed Stars At the beginning of Chongzhen, Minister of Rites Xu Guangqi supervised revision of the calendar law and submitted the 'General Star Map of the Visible Horizon.'
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Fixed Stars Early in the Chongzhen reign, Xu Guangqi, minister of rites, oversaw calendar reform and presented the General Star Map of the Visible Horizon.

sentences.zh: 以為回回《立成》所載，有黃道經緯度者止二百七十八星，其繪圖者止十七座九十四星，並無赤道經緯。

translations.literal: He considered that in the Islamic Licheng what was recorded with ecliptic longitude and latitude numbered only two hundred seventy-eight stars; what was drawn numbered only seventeen asterisms ninety-four stars—and there were no equatorial coordinates at all.
translations.idiomatic: He noted that the Islamic Licheng tables listed ecliptic coordinates for only 278 stars and illustrated only 17 asterisms (94 stars), with no equatorial coordinates whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 今皆崇禎元年所測，黃赤二道經緯度畢具。

translations.literal: Now all are measured in Chongzhen year one; yellow and red two paths' longitude and latitude are completely provided.
translations.idiomatic: The present survey, completed in Chongzhen 1, supplies both ecliptic and equatorial coordinates throughout.

sentences.zh: 後又上《赤道兩總星圖》。

translations.literal: Later he again submitted the 'Two General Star Maps of the Equator.'
translations.idiomatic: He later submitted the Two General Star Maps of the Equator.

sentences.zh: 其說謂常現常隱之界，隨北極高下而殊，圖不能限。

translations.literal: Its doctrine says the boundary of always visible and always hidden follows the north pole's height and differs; a map cannot limit it.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the always-visible and always-hidden zones shift with the observer's latitude and cannot be fixed on a single chart.

sentences.zh: 且天度近極則漸狹，而《見界圖》從赤道以南，其度反寬，所繪星座不合仰觀。

translations.literal: Moreover celestial degrees near the pole gradually narrow, yet the Visible-Horizon Map south of the equator has degrees instead wider; the drawn constellations do not match looking up.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, degrees crowd narrower near the poles, yet south of the equator the Visible-Horizon Map spreads them wider—so its constellations do not match what one sees overhead.

sentences.zh: 因從赤道中剖渾天為二，一以北極為心，一以南極為心。

translations.literal: Therefore from the equator the armillary heaven was bisected in two—one with the north pole as center, one with the south pole as center.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore split the celestial globe at the equator into two charts, one centered on the north pole and one on the south.

sentences.zh: 從心至周，皆九十度，合之得一百八十度者，赤道緯度也。

translations.literal: From center to circumference all ninety degrees; combined obtaining one hundred eighty degrees—this is equatorial latitude.
translations.idiomatic: From each pole to the circumference is ninety degrees; the two hemispheres together make 180 degrees of equatorial latitude.

sentences.zh: 周分三百六十度者，赤道經度也。

translations.literal: The circumference divided into three hundred sixty degrees is equatorial longitude.
translations.idiomatic: The full 360 degrees around the circumference is equatorial longitude.

sentences.zh: 乃依各星之經緯點之，遠近位置形勢皆合天象。

translations.literal: Then according to each star's longitude and latitude points were placed; far and near, position and form all match celestial signs.
translations.idiomatic: Stars were plotted at their coordinate points so that distance, placement, and configuration all matched the sky.

sentences.zh: 至於恆星循黃道右旋，惟黃道緯度無古今之異，而赤道經緯則歲歲不同。

translations.literal: As for fixed stars following the ecliptic in rightward revolution, only ecliptic latitude has no ancient–modern difference, while equatorial longitude and latitude differ year by year.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed stars drift eastward along the ecliptic; ecliptic latitude is unchanged from antiquity, but equatorial coordinates shift annually.

sentences.zh: 然亦有黃赤俱差，甚至前後易次者。

translations.literal: Yet there are also both yellow and red differing, even to the point that front and back exchange order.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes both ecliptic and equatorial coordinates shift enough to reverse the order of neighboring asterisms.

sentences.zh: 如觜宿距星，唐測在參前三度，元測在參前五分，今測已侵入參宿。

translations.literal: For example the Turtle-Beak lodge determining star: Tang measurement placed it three degrees before Three Stars; Yuan measurement five fen before Three Stars; present measurement has already intruded into Three Stars lodge.
translations.idiomatic: The determining star of Zi xiu (Turtle Beak): Tang observers placed it 3° ahead of Shen (Three Stars); Yuan observers 5 fen ahead; the present survey finds it inside Shen.

sentences.zh: 故舊法先觜後參，今不得不先參後觜，不可強也。

translations.literal: Therefore the old method first Turtle-Beak then Three Stars; today one cannot but first Three Stars then Turtle-Beak—cannot be forced.
translations.idiomatic: Older tables listed Zi before Shen; today Shen must precede Zi—no convention can override observation.

sentences.zh: 又有古多今少，古有今無者。

translations.literal: Again there are ancient many today few, ancient have today none.
translations.idiomatic: Some asterisms counted more stars in antiquity than now; others recorded then have vanished.

sentences.zh: 如紫微垣中六甲六星今止有一，華蓋十六星今止有四，傳捨九星今五，天廚六星今五，天牢六星今二。

translations.literal: For example in Purple Forbidden Enclosure the six Jia six stars today only have one; Canopy sixteen stars today only four; Relay Lodges nine stars today five; Celestial Kitchen six stars today five; Celestial Prison six stars today two.
translations.idiomatic: In the Purple Forbidden Enclosure, for instance: the six Jia stars are now one; Canopy (Huagai), 16 stars now 4; Relay Lodges (Chuanshe), 9 now 5; Celestial Kitchen (Tianchu), 6 now 5; Celestial Prison (Tianlao), 6 now 2.

sentences.zh: 又如天理、四勢、五帝內座、天柱、天床、大贊府、大理、女御、內廚，皆全無也。

translations.literal: Again Heavenly Principle, Four Supports, Five Emperors Inner Seat, Celestial Pillar, Celestial Bed, Great Praise Office, Great Adjudication, Female Attendants, Inner Kitchen—all completely without.
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly Principle, Four Supports, Five Emperors Inner Seat, Celestial Pillar, Celestial Bed, Great Praise Office, Great Adjudication, Female Attendants, and Inner Kitchen—entirely gone.

sentences.zh: 天市垣之市樓六星今二。

translations.literal: Heavenly Market Enclosure's Market Tower six stars today two.
translations.idiomatic: In the Heavenly Market Enclosure, Market Tower: 6 stars anciently, 2 today.

sentences.zh: 太微垣之常陳七星今三，郎位十五星今十。

translations.literal: Supreme Palace Enclosure's Regular Array seven stars today three; Court Gentlemen fifteen stars today ten.
translations.idiomatic: In the Supreme Palace Enclosure, Regular Array: 7 stars now 3; Court Gentlemen (Langwei): 15 now 10.

sentences.zh: 長垣四星今二。

translations.literal: Long Wall four stars today two.
translations.idiomatic: Long Wall: 4 stars anciently, 2 today.

translations.idiomatic: Conversely, some stars appear now that antiquity did not record.

sentences.zh: 策星旁有客星，萬歷元年新出，先大今小。

translations.literal: Beside the Whip star there is a guest star; Wanli year one newly appeared, first large now small.
translations.idiomatic: Beside the Whip (Ce) star a guest star appeared in Wanli 1—bright at first, now faint.

sentences.zh: 南極諸星，古所未有，近年浮海之人至赤道以南，往往見之，因測其經緯度。

translations.literal: South Pole various stars, antiquity never had them; in recent years those who float on the sea to south of the equator often see them, therefore their longitude and latitude were measured.
translations.idiomatic: Stars around the south celestial pole were unknown to the ancients; mariners crossing the equator in recent years have sighted them, and their coordinates have been measured.

sentences.zh: 其余增入之星甚多，並詳《恆星表》。

translations.literal: The rest of added stars are very many; all are detailed in the 'Fixed-Star Tables.'
translations.idiomatic: Many further stars have been added; see the Fixed-Star Tables for particulars.

sentences.zh: 其論雲漢，起尾宿，分兩派。

translations.literal: Its discussion of the River of Heaven begins at Tail lodge and divides into two branches.
translations.idiomatic: On the Milky Way: it rises at Wei xiu (Tail) and splits into two branches.

sentences.zh: 一經天江、南海、市樓，過宗人、宗星，涉天津至螣蛇。

translations.literal: One passes Heavenly River, South Sea, Market Tower, crosses Clan Person and Clan Star, fords Tianjin to Flying Serpent.
translations.idiomatic: One branch runs through Tianjiang (Heavenly River), Nanhai (South Sea), and Shilou (Market Tower), past Zongren (Clan Person) and Zongxing (Clan Star), crosses Tianjin, and reaches Tengshe (Flying Serpent).

sentences.zh: 一由箕、斗、天弁、河鼓、左右旗，涉天津至車府而會於螣蛇，過造父，直趨附路、閣道、大陵、天船，漸下而南行，歷五車、天關、司怪、水府，傍東井，入四瀆，過闕丘、弧矢、天狗之墟，抵天社、海石之南，逾南船，帶海山，置十字架、蜜蜂，傍馬腹，經南門，絡三角、龜、杵，而屬於尾宿，是為帶天一周。

translations.literal: One branch runs from Winnowing Basket and Dipper, through Celestial Flank, River Drum, and the Left and Right Banners, crosses Celestial Ford to Chariot Office and meets at Flying Serpent; passes Zaofu, strikes straight for Attached Road, Cloud Path, Great Mound, and Celestial Boat; gradually descends south, passes Five Chariots, Celestial Pass, Director of Oddities, and Water Office; skirts Eastern Well, enters the Four Streams, crosses the mounds of Que Hill, Bow and Arrow, and Celestial Dog, reaches south of Celestial Altar and Sea Rock, crosses Southern Boat, spans Sea Mountain, sets Crux and the Beehive, flanks Horse's Belly, passes Southern Gate, links Triangle, Tortoise, and Pestle, and joins Tail lodge—thus girdling heaven once around.
translations.idiomatic: The second branch runs from Winnowing Basket and the Dipper through Celestial Flank, River Drum, and the Left and Right Banners, crosses Celestial Ford to Chariot Office and converges at Flying Serpent; it passes Zaofu and drives straight toward Attached Road, Cloud Path, Great Mound, and Celestial Boat, then slopes south by degrees through Five Chariots, Celestial Pass, Director of Oddities, and Water Office, skirts Eastern Well, enters the Four Streams, crosses the grounds of Que Hill, Bow and Arrow, and Celestial Dog, reaches the south of Celestial Altar and Sea Rock, crosses Southern Boat and spans Sea Mountain, sets Crux and the Beehive beside Horse's Belly, passes Southern Gate, links Triangle, Tortoise, and Pestle, and rejoins Tail lodge—completing one circuit about the sky.

sentences.zh: 以理推之，隱界自應有雲漢，其所見當不誣。

translations.literal: Reasoning it out, the hidden realm ought naturally to have a Cloud River, and what is seen should not be false.
translations.idiomatic: By reason alone, the hidden hemisphere ought to carry a Milky Way as well; what observers see should not be deceiving.

sentences.zh: 又謂雲漢為無數小星，大陵鬼宿中積屍亦然。

translations.literal: It is also said that the Cloud River consists of countless small stars, and that the Accumulated Corpses in Ghost lodge within Great Mound are the same.
translations.idiomatic: They also hold that the Milky Way is made of innumerable small stars, and that the Accumulated Corpses in Ghost lodge within Great Mound are likewise so.

sentences.zh: 考《天官書》言星漢皆金之散氣，則星漢本同類，得此可以相證。

translations.literal: Examining the Treatise on the Heavenly Offices, which says that the starry stream is scattered qi of metal, star stream and Cloud River are of the same kind—this can serve as mutual proof.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on the Heavenly Offices says the starry stream is scattered essence of metal; the star stream and the Milky Way belong to the same class, and the present findings confirm it.

sentences.zh: 又言昴宿有三十六星，皆得之於窺遠鏡者。

translations.literal: It is also said that Hairy Head lodge has thirty-six stars, all obtained by the far-viewing tube.
translations.idiomatic: They further report thirty-six stars in Hairy Head lodge, every one revealed through the telescope.

sentences.zh: 凡測而入表之星共一千三百四十七，微細無名者不與。

translations.literal: In all, stars measured and entered in the tables number one thousand three hundred forty-seven; fine stars without names are not included.
translations.idiomatic: Stars measured and entered in the tables total one thousand three hundred forty-seven; faint stars without established names are omitted.

sentences.zh: 其大小分為六等：內一等十六星，二等六十七星，三等二百零七星，四等五百零三星，五等三百三十八星，六等二百一十六星。

translations.literal: By size they are divided into six grades: within, first grade sixteen stars, second grade sixty-seven stars, third grade two hundred seven stars, fourth grade five hundred three stars, fifth grade three hundred thirty-eight stars, sixth grade two hundred sixteen stars.
translations.idiomatic: By apparent size they fall into six grades: first magnitude, sixteen stars; second, sixty-seven; third, two hundred seven; fourth, five hundred three; fifth, three hundred thirty-eight; sixth, two hundred sixteen.

sentences.zh: 悉具黃赤二道經緯度。

translations.literal: All are furnished with longitude and latitude on the yellow and red paths.
translations.idiomatic: Each is given ecliptic and equatorial longitude and latitude.

sentences.zh: 列表二卷，入光啟所修《崇禎歷書》中。

translations.literal: Two scrolls of tables were compiled and entered into the Chongzhen Reign Treatise on the Calendar that Guangqi revised.
translations.idiomatic: The work fills two scrolls of tables, incorporated into the Chongzhen Reign Treatise on the Calendar that Xu Guangqi helped compile.

sentences.zh: 茲取二十八宿距星及一二等大星存之，其小而有名者，間取一二，備列左方。

translations.literal: Here we take the twenty-eight lodges' distance stars and stars of the first and second grades and preserve them; for small stars that still have names, one or two are occasionally taken and set out on the left.
translations.idiomatic: What follows retains the twenty-eight lodges' determinant stars and all stars of the first and second magnitude; among smaller stars that still bear names, only a sample of one or two is listed at left for reference.

sentences.zh: 表格略

translations.literal: Tables abbreviated.
translations.idiomatic: The tables are abbreviated here.

sentences.zh: ▲黃赤宿度 崇禎元年所測二十八宿黃赤度分，皆不合於古。

translations.literal: ▲ Yellow-red lodge degrees: the yellow-red degree-minutes of the twenty-eight lodges measured in Chongzhen year one all fail to agree with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Yellow and red lodge degrees: the ecliptic and equatorial degree-minutes of the twenty-eight lodges measured in the first year of the Chongzhen reign all diverge from ancient values.

sentences.zh: 夫星既依黃道行，而赤道與黃道斜交，其度不能無增減者，勢也。

translations.literal: Now stars follow the yellow path in their motion, while the red path and yellow path cross obliquely; that their degrees cannot be without increase and decrease is the tendency of things.
translations.idiomatic: Since stars move along the ecliptic while the equator cuts it obliquely, their measured degrees cannot but shift—a matter of geometry, not error alone.

sentences.zh: 而黃道度亦有增減者，或推測有得失，抑恆星之行亦或各有遲速歟。

translations.literal: Yet yellow-path degrees also show increase and decrease—perhaps there are gains and losses in calculation, or perhaps the motion of fixed stars too may each have its own slowness and speed.
translations.idiomatic: Ecliptic degrees likewise show increase and decrease: this may reflect mistakes in computation, or it may mean that fixed stars themselves advance at unequal rates.

sentences.zh: 謹列其數，以備參考。

translations.literal: We carefully set out the figures below for reference.
translations.idiomatic: The figures are set out below for consultation.
