translations.literal: Chariot Axle, fifteen degrees thirty minutes.
translations.idiomatic: Chariot Axle on the equator: fifteen degrees thirty minutes.

sentences.zh: 一十三度零三分。

translations.literal: Thirteen degrees three minutes.
translations.idiomatic: Chariot Axle on the ecliptic: thirteen degrees three minutes.

sentences.zh: ▲黃赤宮界 十二宮之名見於《爾雅》，大抵皆依星宿而定。

translations.literal: ▲ Yellow-red palace boundaries: the names of the twelve palaces appear in the Erya, and for the most part they are fixed by star lodges.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Yellow and red palace boundaries: the twelve celestial palaces are named in the Erya, and for the most part each name is anchored to particular lodges.

sentences.zh: 如婁、奎為降婁，心為大火，硃鳥七宿為鶉首、鶉尾之類。

translations.literal: For example Bond and Striding Legs are Lower Harvester; Heart is Great Fire; the seven lodges of the Vermilion Bird are Quail Head, Quail Tail, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Bond and Striding Legs mark Lower Harvester; Heart marks Great Fire; the Vermilion Bird's seven lodges yield Quail Head, Quail Tail, and their sister palaces.

sentences.zh: 故宮有一定之宿，宿有常居之宮，由來尚矣。

translations.literal: Thus palaces have fixed lodges, and lodges have their constant palaces—this has long been so.
translations.idiomatic: Each palace therefore owned fixed lodges, and each lodge had its habitual palace—a correspondence honored since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 唐以後始用歲差，然亦天自為天，歲自為歲，宮與星仍舊不易。

translations.literal: After the Tang they began to use precession, yet heaven remains heaven and the year remains the year; palaces and stars were still not changed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tang, astronomers acknowledged precession, yet heaven was still heaven and the year still the year; palace names and star positions were left unchanged in practice.

sentences.zh: 西洋之法，以中氣過宮，如日躔冬至，即為星紀宮之類。

translations.literal: In the Western method, when a middle qi passes a palace—as when the sun's station is winter solstice, that is the Xingji palace, and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: Western method ties each palace to the middle qi that crosses it: when the sun stands at winter solstice, for example, the palace is Xingji.

sentences.zh: 而恆星既有歲進之差，於是宮無定宿，而宿可以遞居各宮，此變古法之大端也。

translations.literal: But fixed stars also have the discrepancy of annual advance; thus palaces have no fixed lodges, and lodges may in turn dwell in each palace in succession—this is the great break with the ancient method.
translations.idiomatic: Because fixed stars drift year by year, palaces no longer keep permanent lodges, and lodges may migrate from palace to palace—this is the decisive departure from ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 茲以崇禎元年各宿交宮之黃赤度，分列於左方，以志權輿雲。

translations.literal: Here the yellow-red degrees at which each lodge crossed a palace in Chongzhen year one are set out on the left, to record the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Below are listed, for the first year of the Chongzhen reign, the ecliptic and equatorial degrees at which each lodge entered its palace—marking the new starting point.

sentences.zh: 赤道交宮宿度 黃道交宮宿度 箕，三度零七分，入星紀。

translations.literal: Red-path palace-crossing lodge degrees; yellow-path palace-crossing lodge degrees: Winnowing Basket, three degrees seven minutes, entering Xingji.
translations.idiomatic: Equatorial degrees where lodges cross palaces; ecliptic degrees where lodges cross palaces—Winnowing Basket at three degrees seven minutes, entering Xingji (equator).

sentences.zh: 箕，四度一十七分，入星紀。

translations.literal: Winnowing Basket, four degrees seventeen minutes, entering Xingji.
translations.idiomatic: Winnowing Basket at four degrees seventeen minutes, entering Xingji (ecliptic).

sentences.zh: 鬥，二十四度二十一分，入玄枵。

translations.literal: Dipper, twenty-four degrees twenty-one minutes, entering Xuanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper at twenty-four degrees twenty-one minutes, entering Xuanyuan (equator).

sentences.zh: 牛，一度零六分，入玄枵 危，三度一十九分，入娵訾。

translations.literal: Ox, one degree six minutes, entering Xuanyuan; Rooftop, three degrees nineteen minutes, entering Ziwei.
translations.idiomatic: Ox at one degree six minutes, entering Xuanyuan (ecliptic); Rooftop at three degrees nineteen minutes, entering Ziwei (equator).

sentences.zh: 危，一度四十七分，入娵訾。

translations.literal: Rooftop, one degree forty-seven minutes, entering Ziwei.
translations.idiomatic: Rooftop at one degree forty-seven minutes, entering Ziwei (ecliptic).

sentences.zh: 壁，一度二十六分，入降婁。

translations.literal: Wall, one degree twenty-six minutes, entering Lower Harvester.
translations.idiomatic: Wall at one degree twenty-six minutes, entering Lower Harvester (equator).

sentences.zh: 室，一十一度四十分，入降婁。

translations.literal: Encampment, eleven degrees forty minutes, entering Lower Harvester.
translations.idiomatic: Encampment at eleven degrees forty minutes, entering Lower Harvester (ecliptic).

sentences.zh: 婁，六度二十八分，入大梁。

translations.literal: Bond, six degrees twenty-eight minutes, entering Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Bond at six degrees twenty-eight minutes, entering Daliang (equator).

sentences.zh: 婁，一度一十四分，入大梁。

translations.literal: Bond, one degree fourteen minutes, entering Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Bond at one degree fourteen minutes, entering Daliang (ecliptic).

sentences.zh: 昴，八度三十九分，入實沈。

translations.literal: Hairy Head, eight degrees thirty-nine minutes, entering Real Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Hairy Head at eight degrees thirty-nine minutes, entering Real Shen (equator).

sentences.zh: 昴，五度一十三分，入實沈。

translations.literal: Hairy Head, five degrees thirteen minutes, entering Real Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Hairy Head at five degrees thirteen minutes, entering Real Shen (ecliptic).

sentences.zh: 觜，一十一度一十七分，入鶉首。

translations.literal: Turtle Beak, eleven degrees seventeen minutes, entering Quail Head.
translations.idiomatic: Turtle Beak at eleven degrees seventeen minutes, entering Quail Head (equator).

sentences.zh: 觜，一十一度二十五分，入鶉首。

translations.literal: Turtle Beak, eleven degrees twenty-five minutes, entering Quail Head.
translations.idiomatic: Turtle Beak at eleven degrees twenty-five minutes, entering Quail Head (ecliptic).

sentences.zh: 井，二十九度五十三分，入鶉火。

translations.literal: Well, twenty-nine degrees fifty-three minutes, entering Quail Fire.
translations.idiomatic: Well at twenty-nine degrees fifty-three minutes, entering Quail Fire (equator).

sentences.zh: 井，二十九度五十二分，入鶉火。

translations.literal: Well, twenty-nine degrees fifty-two minutes, entering Quail Fire.
translations.idiomatic: Well at twenty-nine degrees fifty-two minutes, entering Quail Fire (ecliptic).

sentences.zh: 張，六度五十一分，入鶉尾。

translations.literal: Extended Net, six degrees fifty-one minutes, entering Quail Tail.
translations.idiomatic: Extended Net at six degrees fifty-one minutes, entering Quail Tail (equator).

sentences.zh: 星，七度五十一分，入鶉尾。

translations.literal: Star, seven degrees fifty-one minutes, entering Quail Tail.
translations.idiomatic: Star at seven degrees fifty-one minutes, entering Quail Tail (ecliptic).

sentences.zh: 翼，一十九度三十二分，入壽星。

translations.literal: Wings, nineteen degrees thirty-two minutes, entering Longevity Star.
translations.idiomatic: Wings at nineteen degrees thirty-two minutes, entering Longevity Star (equator).

sentences.zh: 翼，一十一度二十四分，入壽星。

translations.literal: Wings, eleven degrees twenty-four minutes, entering Longevity Star.
translations.idiomatic: Wings at eleven degrees twenty-four minutes, entering Longevity Star (ecliptic).

sentences.zh: 亢，一度五十分，入大火。

translations.literal: Neck, one degree fifty minutes, entering Great Fire.
translations.idiomatic: Neck at one degree fifty minutes, entering Great Fire (equator).

sentences.zh: 亢，初度四十六分，入大火。

translations.literal: Neck, at the first degree forty-six minutes, entering Great Fire.
translations.idiomatic: Neck at the lodge's first degree forty-six minutes, entering Great Fire (ecliptic).

sentences.zh: 心，初度二十二分，入析木。

translations.literal: Heart: at its initial degree, twenty-two parts; it enters Split Wood.
translations.idiomatic: The Heart lodge, at its initial degree of twenty-two parts, enters Split Wood.

sentences.zh: 房，二度一十二分，入析木。

translations.literal: Room: at two degrees, twelve parts; it enters Split Wood.
translations.idiomatic: The Room lodge, at two degrees and twelve parts, enters Split Wood.

sentences.zh: ▲儀象

translations.literal: ▲ Armillary Sphere and Celestial Globe
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Armillary Sphere and Celestial Globe

sentences.zh: 璇璣玉衡為儀象之權輿，然不見用於三代。

translations.literal: The armillary of jade transparencies was the origin of armillary spheres and celestial globes, yet it was not used in the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The armillary of jade transparencies was the wellspring of armillary spheres and celestial globes, yet the Three Dynasties never put it to use.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》有圭表、壺漏，而無璣衡，其制遂不可考。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou has the gnomon table and clepsydra, but no armillary; its design can no longer be verified.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou records the gnomon table and clepsydra but not the armillary, and its form can no longer be recovered.

sentences.zh: 漢人創造渾天儀，謂即璣衡遺制，其或然歟。

translations.literal: Han men created the armillary heaven instrument, saying it was the surviving design of the armillary; this may be so.
translations.idiomatic: Han craftsmen devised the armillary heaven instrument, claiming it as the armillary’s surviving design—and they may have been right.

sentences.zh: 厥後代有制作。

translations.literal: Thereafter each age had its own productions.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every age produced instruments of its own.

sentences.zh: 大抵以六合、三辰、四游、重環湊合者，謂之渾天儀；

translations.literal: Generally those assembled from the Six Harmonies, Three Luminaries, Four Excursions, and multiple rings were called armillary heaven instruments;
translations.idiomatic: In general, instruments built up from the Six Harmonies, Three Luminaries, Four Excursions, and nested rings were called armillary heaven instruments;

sentences.zh: 以實體圓球，繪黃赤經緯度，或綴以星宿者，謂之渾天象。

translations.literal: those of solid sphere painted with ecliptic and equatorial longitudes and latitudes, sometimes set with star lodges, were called armillary heaven images.
translations.idiomatic: those fashioned as solid spheres painted with ecliptic and equatorial coordinates, sometimes studded with lodges, were called armillary heaven images.

sentences.zh: 其制雖有詳略，要亦青藍之別也。

translations.literal: Though their designs differed in detail and summary, in essentials they were but variations in shade of blue.
translations.idiomatic: Though their designs differed in fineness and scope, in essence they were only shades of the same indigo.

sentences.zh: 外此則圭表、壺漏而已。

translations.literal: Beyond these there were only the gnomon table and clepsydra.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these there remained only the gnomon table and clepsydra.

sentences.zh: 迨元作簡儀、仰儀、窺幾、景符之屬，制器始精詳矣。

translations.literal: When the Yuan made the simplified instrument, azimuth instrument, sighting gauge, shadow tablet, and the like, instrument-making first became truly precise and detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan, with the simplified instrument, azimuth instrument, sighting gauge, shadow tablet, and their kind, the craft of instruments first grew truly precise.

sentences.zh: 明太祖平元，司天監進水晶刻漏，中設二木偶人，能按時自擊鉦鼓。

translations.literal: When the Ming Founder pacified the Yuan, the Directorate of Astronomy presented a crystal clepsydra with two puppet figures inside that could strike bells and drums on their own according to the hour.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming Founder pacified the Yuan, the Directorate of Astronomy presented a crystal clepsydra fitted with two puppet figures that could strike bells and drums by themselves at the proper hours.

sentences.zh: 太祖以其無益而碎之。

translations.literal: The Founder found it useless and smashed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder judged it worthless and had it smashed.

sentences.zh: 洪武十七年，造觀星盤。

translations.literal: Hongwu year 17: an observational star disk was made.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year seventeen an observational star disk was made.

sentences.zh: 十八年，設觀象台於雞鳴山。

translations.literal: Year 18: an Observatory was established on Cockcrow Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen an observatory was established on Cockcrow Mountain.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，鑄渾天儀。

translations.literal: Year 24: an armillary sphere was cast.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four an armillary sphere was cast.

sentences.zh: 正統二年，行在欽天監正皇甫仲和奏言：「南京觀象台設渾天儀、簡儀、圭表以窺測七政行度，而北京乃止於齊化門城上觀測，未有儀象。

translations.literal: Zhengtong year 2, the acting director at the capital Huangfu Zhonghe memorialized: "At the Nanjing Observatory there are set up an armillary sphere, simplified instrument, and gnomon table to observe the degrees in the motion of the seven luminaries, whereas at Beijing observation is made only from atop the Qi Gate wall, without armillary instruments.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year two, Huangfu Zhonghe, acting director of the Directorate at the capital, memorialized: "At the Nanjing Observatory an armillary sphere, simplified instrument, and gnomon table are installed to measure the courses of the seven luminaries, yet at Beijing we observe only from atop the Qi Gate wall, with no armillary instruments at all.

sentences.zh: 乞令本監官往南京，用木做造，挈赴北京，以較驗北極出地高下，然後用銅別鑄，庶幾占測有憑。

translations.literal: I beg that officials of this directorate be sent to Nanjing to make wooden copies and bring them to Beijing, to compare the height of the north pole above the horizon, and then cast separately in bronze, so that observation and divination may have a basis."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that officials of this directorate go to Nanjing, reproduce them in wood, and carry them to Beijing to compare how high the north pole stands above the horizon here; only then should separate bronze castings be made, so that observation and divination may rest on firm ground."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court assented.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，乃鑄銅渾天儀、簡儀於北京。

translations.literal: Next winter bronze armillary sphere and simplified instrument were cast at Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter bronze armillary sphere and simplified instrument were cast at Beijing.

sentences.zh: 御制《觀天器銘》。

translations.literal: The emperor composed the "Inscription on the Heaven-Observing Apparatus."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor composed the "Inscription on the Heaven-Observing Apparatus."

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：「粵古大聖，體天施治，敬天以心，觀天以器。

translations.literal: Its words run: "Of old the great sages embodied Heaven in governing, revered Heaven in the heart, and observed Heaven through instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Its words run: "In antiquity the great sages embodied Heaven in their rule, revered Heaven in the heart, and read Heaven through instruments.

sentences.zh: 厥器伊何？

translations.literal: What instrument was it?
translations.idiomatic: What instrument was it?

sentences.zh: 璇璣玉衡。

translations.literal: The armillary of jade transparencies.
translations.idiomatic: The armillary of jade transparencies.

sentences.zh: 璣象天體，衡審天行。

translations.literal: The armillary mirrors the celestial body; the balance adjudicates celestial motion.
translations.idiomatic: The armillary mirrors the body of Heaven; the balance weighs the motion of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 歷世代更，垂四千祀，沿制有作，其制寢備。

translations.literal: Age after age it was renewed, spanning four thousand years; along the inherited design improvements were made until the design was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Dynasty after dynasty renewed it across four thousand years; along the inherited design work was added until the design stood complete.

sentences.zh: 即器而觀，六合外儀，陽經陰緯，方位可稽。

translations.literal: Observing through the instrument, the outer frame of the Six Harmonies, yang tracks and yin tracks, positions may be reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: Through the instrument one views the outer frame of the Six Harmonies—yang tracks and yin tracks—so that positions may be reckoned.

sentences.zh: 中儀三辰，黃赤二道，日月暨星，運行可考。

translations.literal: The inner frame of the Three Luminaries, the two tracks of yellow and red, sun, moon, and stars—their courses may be examined.
translations.idiomatic: The inner frame of the Three Luminaries, the two tracks of yellow and red: sun, moon, and stars—their courses may be examined.

sentences.zh: 內儀四游，橫簫中貫，南北東西，低昂旋轉。

translations.literal: The innermost frame of the Four Excursions, a transverse tube pierced through the center—north, south, east, and west, rising and sinking in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: The innermost frame of the Four Excursions: a transverse tube pierced through the center—north, south, east, and west, sinking and rising in turn.

sentences.zh: 簡儀之作，爰代璣衡，制約用密，疏朗而精。

translations.literal: When the simplified instrument was made it replaced the armillary; compact in design yet open and precise.
translations.idiomatic: When the simplified instrument was fashioned it took the armillary’s place—tighter in design, yet spare and exact.

sentences.zh: 外有渾象，反而觀諸，上規下矩，度數方隅。

translations.literal: Outside there is the armillary image, viewed in reverse; upper compass and lower square, degrees and cardinal directions.
translations.idiomatic: Outside stands the armillary image, viewed in reverse; compass above and square below, degrees and cardinal directions.

sentences.zh: 別有直表，其崇八尺，分至氣序，考景鹹得。

translations.literal: Separately there is the vertical table, eight feet high; solstices and qi seasons—all shadows may be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from these is the vertical table, eight feet tall; solstices and seasonal qi—all shadows may be taken from it.

sentences.zh: 縣象在天，制器在人，測驗推步，靡忒毫分。

translations.literal: The image is hung in Heaven; the instrument is made by man; measurement and stepwise calculation err not by a hair’s fraction.
translations.idiomatic: The image hangs in Heaven; the instrument is wrought by man; measurement and stepwise reckoning miss not a hair’s breadth.

sentences.zh: 昔作今述，為制彌工，既明且悉，用將無窮。

translations.literal: What the ancients made, what we now describe—the design grows more skilled, clear and thorough, for endless use.
translations.idiomatic: What the ancients made and what we now set down—the craft grows finer, lucid and complete, fit for endless use.

sentences.zh: 惟天勤民，事天首務，民不失寧，天其予顧。

translations.literal: Heaven is diligent on behalf of the people; serving Heaven is the first task; if the people know no unrest, Heaven will regard us.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven labors for the people; to serve Heaven is the first duty; if the people are not disturbed, Heaven will look upon us.

sentences.zh: 政純於仁，天道以正，勒銘斯器，以勵予敬。

translations.literal: When government is pure in benevolence, the Way of Heaven is rectified; we inscribe this instrument to encourage our reverence."
translations.idiomatic: When rule is pure in benevolence, Heaven’s Way is set right; we inscribe this instrument to quicken our reverence."

sentences.zh: 」十一年，監臣言：「簡儀未刻度數，且地基卑下，窺測日星，為四面台宇所蔽。

translations.literal: Year 11, directorate officials said: "The simplified instrument has not been marked with degree numbers, and its foundation is low; in observing sun and stars it is obstructed on all four sides by terrace buildings.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven directorate officials said: "The simplified instrument has not been graduated, and its platform sits too low; when we observe sun and stars, terrace buildings block us on every side.

sentences.zh: 圭表置露台，光皆四散，影無定則。

translations.literal: The gnomon table is set on a terrace; light scatters on every side and the shadow has no fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: The gnomon table stands on a terrace; light scatters on all sides and the shadow has no fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 壺漏屋低，夜天池促，難以注水調品時刻。

translations.literal: The clepsydra house is low and the night-celestial pool cramped, making it hard to pour water and regulate the gradations of the hours.
translations.idiomatic: The clepsydra house is low and the night-celestial pool cramped, so it is hard to pour water and tune the hour-gradations.

sentences.zh: 請更如法修造。

translations.literal: Request rebuilding according to the proper method."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that these be rebuilt according to regulation."

sentences.zh: 」報可。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，監正彭德清又言：「北京北極出地度、太陽出入時刻與南京不同，冬夏晝長夜短亦異。

translations.literal: Next winter Director Peng Deqing again said: "Beijing’s degree of the north pole above the horizon and the times of the sun’s rising and setting differ from Nanjing’s; winter and summer day length and night shortness also differ.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter Director Peng Deqing again said: "Beijing’s north-pole altitude and the times of the sun’s rising and setting differ from Nanjing’s; winter days and summer nights are likewise not the same length.

sentences.zh: 今宮禁及官府漏箭皆南京舊式，不可用。

translations.literal: Now the clepsydra arrows in the palace and government offices are all in the old Nanjing pattern and cannot be used."
translations.idiomatic: The clepsydra arrows now used in the palace precinct and government offices are all in the old Nanjing pattern and will not serve."

sentences.zh: 」有旨，令內官監改造。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Directorate of Palace Manufactories to remake them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Directorate of Palace Manufactories to remake them.

sentences.zh: 景泰六年又造內觀象台簡儀及銅壺。

translations.literal: Jingtai year 6 they again made a simplified instrument and bronze clepsydra for the inner observatory.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai year six a simplified instrument and bronze clepsydra were again made for the inner observatory.

sentences.zh: 成化中，尚書周洪謨復請造璇璣玉衡，憲宗令自制以進。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua reign Minister Zhou Hongmo again requested making an armillary of jade transparencies; Xianzong ordered him to make it himself and present it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign Minister Zhou Hongmo again petitioned to make an armillary of jade transparencies; Emperor Xianzong ordered him to craft it himself and present it.

sentences.zh: 十四年，監臣請修晷影堂，從之。

translations.literal: Year 14, directorate officials requested repairing the gnomon-shadow hall; approved.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen directorate officials asked to repair the gnomon-shadow hall; the court assented.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年，監正吳昊言：「考驗四正日度，黃赤二道應交於壁軫。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 2, Director Wu Hao said: "In verifying the sun’s positions at the four cardinal points, the yellow and red tracks ought to intersect at Wall and Axletree.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi year two Director Wu Hao said: "When we verify the sun’s positions at the four cardinal points, the yellow and red tracks should intersect at Wall and Axletree.

sentences.zh: 觀象台舊制渾儀，黃赤二道交於奎軫，不合天象，其南北兩軸不合兩極出入之度，窺管又不與太陽出沒相當，故雖設而不用。

translations.literal: The old armillary on the observatory has yellow and red tracks intersecting at Stride and Axletree, not matching the heavens; its north and south axes do not match the degrees of the two poles’ rising and setting, and the sighting tube does not align with the sun’s emergence and disappearance—therefore though set up it is not used.
translations.idiomatic: The old armillary on the observatory has them intersecting at Stride and Axletree, which does not match the sky; its north and south axes do not match the poles’ rising and setting, and the sighting tube does not line up with the sun’s emergence and disappearance—so though it stands there, we do not use it.

sentences.zh: 所用簡儀則郭守敬遺制，而北極雲柱差短，以測經星去極，亦不能無爽。

translations.literal: The simplified instrument in use is Guo Shoujing’s surviving design, yet the cloud pillar of the north pole is slightly short; in measuring the lodges’ distance from the pole there is still some error.
translations.idiomatic: The simplified instrument we use is Guo Shoujing’s surviving design, but the cloud pillar at the north pole is a little short; when we measure how far lodges stand from the pole, error still creeps in.

sentences.zh: 請修改或別造，以成一代之制。

translations.literal: Request modification or new construction to complete the instruments of the age."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that it be altered or newly cast, to complete this dynasty’s instruments."

sentences.zh: 」事下禮部，覆議令監副張紳造木樣，以待試驗，黃道度許修改焉。

translations.literal: The matter went to the Ministry of Rites, which reported back ordering Vice-Director Zhang Shen to make a wooden model for trial, and that the ecliptic degrees might be modified.
translations.idiomatic: The matter went to the Ministry of Rites, which replied that Vice-Director Zhang Shen should make a wooden model for testing, and that the ecliptic degrees might be adjusted.

sentences.zh: 正德十六年，漏刻博士硃裕復言：「晷表尺寸不一，難以准測，而推算歷數用南京日出分秒，似相矛盾。

translations.literal: Zhengde year 16, clepsydra doctor Zhu Yu again said: "Gnomon tables differ in size and are hard to use as standard measure, while the reckoning of calendar numbers uses Nanjing sunrise minutes and seconds—seemingly contradictory.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde year sixteen Clepsydra Doctor Zhu Yu again said: "Gnomon tables differ in size and cannot serve as a single standard, yet calendar reckoning uses Nanjing sunrise minutes and seconds—as if the two methods contradicted each other.

sentences.zh: 請敕大臣一員總理其事，鑄立銅表，考四時日中之影。

translations.literal: Request an edict to one senior minister to oversee the matter, cast and set up a bronze table, and examine the noon shadow at the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that one senior minister be charged to oversee the work: cast and erect a bronze table and measure the noon shadow through the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 仍於河南陽城察舊立土圭，以合今日之晷，及分立圭表於山東、湖廣、陝西、大名等處，以測四方之影。

translations.literal: Also inspect the old earthen gnomon set up at Yangcheng in Henan to harmonize with today’s gnomon, and separately set up gnomon tables in Shandong, Huguang, Shaanxi, Daming, and elsewhere to measure shadows in the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Also examine the old earthen gnomon at Yangcheng in Henan and bring it into accord with today’s gnomon; and set up separate gnomon tables in Shandong, Huguang, Shaanxi, Daming, and other places to measure shadows in the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 然後將內外晷影新舊歷書錯綜參驗，撰成定法，庶幾天行合而交食不謬。

translations.literal: Then cross-check the old and new calendar books of inner and outer gnomon shadows comprehensively, compose a fixed method, so that celestial motion may agree and eclipse conjunctions not err."
translations.idiomatic: Then cross-check the old and new calendar records of gnomon shadows inside and out, compose a fixed method, and so bring celestial motion into accord and keep eclipse conjunctions from going astray."

sentences.zh: 」疏入不報。

translations.literal: Memorial entered; no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was filed; no answer came.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年修相風桿及簡、渾二儀。

translations.literal: Jiajing year 2: the wind-indicating pole and the simplified and armillary instruments were repaired.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year two the wind-indicating pole and the simplified and armillary instruments were repaired.

sentences.zh: 七年始立四丈木表以測晷影，定氣朔。

translations.literal: Year 7 they first set up a forty-chi wooden table to measure gnomon shadow and fix qi and new moon.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven a forty-chi wooden table was first erected to measure gnomon shadow and fix qi and new moon.

sentences.zh: 由是欽天監之立運儀、正方案、懸晷、偏晷、盤晷諸式具備於觀象台，一以元法為斷。

translations.literal: Hence the Directorate’s revolving instrument, azimuth plate, suspended gnomon, oblique gnomon, dial gnomon, and other forms were all complete on the observatory, taking Yuan methods as sole standard.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Directorate’s revolving instrument, azimuth plate, suspended gnomon, oblique gnomon, dial gnomon, and other forms were all in place on the observatory, with Yuan methods taken as the sole standard.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，西洋人利瑪竇制渾儀、天球、地球等器。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign the Westerner Matteo Ricci made armillary sphere, celestial globe, terrestrial globe, and other instruments.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli reign the Westerner Matteo Ricci made armillary spheres, celestial globes, terrestrial globes, and other instruments.

sentences.zh: 仁和李之藻撰《渾天儀說》，發明制造施用之法，文多不載。

translations.literal: Li Zhizao of Renhe wrote "Explanation of the Armillary Sphere," expounding methods of manufacture and use; the text is mostly not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhizao of Renhe wrote the Explanation of the Armillary Sphere, setting forth how to make and use them; most of that text is not recorded here.

sentences.zh: 其制不外於六合、三辰、四游之法。

translations.literal: The design was nothing beyond the methods of Six Harmonies, Three Luminaries, and Four Excursions.
translations.idiomatic: The design did not go beyond the methods of Six Harmonies, Three Luminaries, and Four Excursions.

sentences.zh: 但古法北極出地，鑄為定度，此則子午提規，可以隨地度高下，於用為便耳。

translations.literal: But in the old method the north pole above the horizon was cast as a fixed degree; in this one the meridian is raised by a rule and can follow the height of the horizon wherever one is—more convenient in use.
translations.idiomatic: In the old method the north-pole altitude was cast as a fixed degree; here the meridian is set by an adjustable rule that can follow the horizon’s height wherever one stands—far more convenient in practice.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，禮部侍郎徐光啟兼理曆法，請造像限大儀六，紀限大儀三，平懸渾儀三，交食儀一，列宿經緯天球一，萬國經緯地球一，平面日晷三，轉盤星晷三，候時鐘三，望遠鏡三。

translations.literal: Chongzhen year 2, Vice Minister of Rites Xu Guangqi concurrently oversaw the calendar and requested six large limit-measuring instruments, three epoch-limit large instruments, three level-suspended armillary instruments, one eclipse instrument, one lodge longitude-latitude celestial globe, one myriad-countries longitude-latitude terrestrial globe, three plane solar gnomons, three revolving star gnomons, three timekeeping clocks, and three telescopes.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year two Vice Minister of Rites Xu Guangqi, who also oversaw the calendar, requested six large limit-measuring instruments, three epoch-limit large instruments, three level-suspended armillary instruments, one eclipse instrument, one lodge longitude-latitude celestial globe, one myriad-countries longitude-latitude terrestrial globe, three plane solar gnomons, three revolving star gnomons, three timekeeping clocks, and three telescopes.

sentences.zh: 報允。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 已，又言：

translations.literal: Having done so, he again said:
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, he spoke again:

sentences.zh: 定時之法，當議者五事：一曰壺漏，二曰指南針，三曰表臬，四曰儀，五曰晷。

translations.literal: The method of fixing time admits five matters for discussion: first, clepsydra; second, compass needle; third, gnomon table; fourth, instrument; fifth, gnomon dial.
translations.idiomatic: On fixing time, five matters must be weighed: first the clepsydra; second the compass needle; third the gnomon table; fourth the instrument; fifth the gnomon dial.

sentences.zh: 漏壺，水有新舊滑濇則遲疾異，漏管有時塞時磷則緩急異。

translations.literal: In the clepsydra, fresh or stale, smooth or rough water makes flow fast or slow; when the outlet is sometimes blocked and sometimes fouled, the drip is sometimes slow and sometimes hurried.
translations.idiomatic: In a clepsydra, fresh or stale, slick or gritty water runs fast or slow; when the outlet is blocked or fouled by turns, the drip slackens or hurries.

sentences.zh: 正漏之初，必於正午初刻。

translations.literal: At the start of correcting the clepsydra one must take the first quarter of noon.
translations.idiomatic: When one first sets a clepsydra right, one must begin at the first quarter of noon.

sentences.zh: 此刻一誤，靡所不誤。

translations.literal: If this moment is wrong, nothing that follows can be right.
translations.idiomatic: Err at that moment, and nothing afterward can be true.

sentences.zh: 故壺漏特以濟晨昏陰晦儀晷表臬所不及，而非定時之本。

translations.literal: Thus the clepsydra serves only to supplement what gnomon dials and tables cannot reach at dawn, dusk, cloud, and gloom—not to be the root of fixing time.
translations.idiomatic: So the clepsydra only fills the gaps left by instruments, gnomon dials, and tables at dawn, dusk, cloud, and gloom—it is not the foundation of fixing time.

sentences.zh: 指南針，術人用以定南北，辨方正位鹹取則焉。

translations.literal: The compass needle: technicians use it to fix north and south; for square positions and bearings it is taken as the rule.
translations.idiomatic: The compass needle: technicians use it to fix north and south, and for bearings and cardinal alignment it is treated as law.

sentences.zh: 然針非指正子午，曩雲多偏丙午之間。

translations.literal: Yet the needle does not point straight at true south and north; formerly it was said to lean mostly toward the wu and zi hours’ direction.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the needle does not aim at true south and north; formerly it was said to lean mostly toward the direction between wu and zi.

sentences.zh: 以法考之，各地不同。

translations.literal: Examined by method, it differs in each place.
translations.idiomatic: Measured by method, it differs from place to place.

sentences.zh: 在京師則偏東五度四十分。

translations.literal: At the capital it leans east by five degrees forty minutes.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital it leans five degrees forty minutes east.

sentences.zh: 若憑以造晷，冬至午正先天一刻四十四分有奇，夏至午正先天五十一分有奇。

translations.literal: If one relied on it to make a gnomon dial, at winter solstice noon it would run ahead of heaven by one quarter and forty-four-odd minutes; at summer solstice noon, ahead by fifty-one-odd minutes.
translations.idiomatic: If one built a gnomon dial by it alone, at winter-solstice noon it would run ahead of heaven by one quarter and forty-four-odd minutes; at summer-solstice noon, ahead by fifty-one-odd minutes.

sentences.zh: 若表臬者，即《考工》匠人置{埶木}之法，識日出入之影，參諸日中之影，以正方位。

translations.literal: As for the gnomon table, it is the method in the Craftsman’s Canon of setting the yi-post, marking the shadow of the sun’s rising and setting and comparing it with the shadow at noon to rectify the cardinal directions.
translations.idiomatic: The gnomon table is the Craftsman’s Canon method of setting the yi-post: one reads the shadows at sunrise and sunset, compares them with the noon shadow, and so rectifies the cardinal directions.

sentences.zh: 今法置小表於地平，午正前後累測日影，以求相等之兩長影為東西，因得中間最短之影為正子午，其術簡甚。

translations.literal: Today’s method sets a small table on level ground, repeatedly measures the sun’s shadow before and after noon to find two equal long shadows as east and west, and from the shortest shadow between them obtains true south-north—the method is very simple.
translations.idiomatic: Today we set a small table on level ground, measure the sun’s shadow repeatedly before and after noon, take two equal long shadows as east and west, and from the shortest shadow between derive true south-north—a method altogether simple.

sentences.zh: 儀者，本台故有立運儀，測驗七政高度。

translations.literal: As for instruments, this directorate already has the revolving instrument for measuring the altitudes of the seven luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: As for instruments, this directorate already possesses the revolving instrument, used to measure the altitudes of the seven luminaries.

sentences.zh: 臣用以較定子午，於午前屢測太陽高度，因最高之度，即得最短之影，是為南北正線。

translations.literal: Your servant used it to fix south-north: before noon I repeatedly measured the sun’s altitude, and from the highest degree obtained the shortest shadow—that is the true north-south line.
translations.idiomatic: I used it to fix south-north: before noon I measured the sun’s altitude again and again; from the highest degree I obtained the shortest shadow—that is the true north-south line.

sentences.zh: 既定子午卯酉之正線，因以法分佈時刻，加入節氣諸線，即成平面日晷。

translations.literal: Once south-north and east-west lines were fixed, I distributed the hours by rule, added the lines of seasonal qi, and so made a plane solar gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: Once the true lines of south-north and east-west were fixed, I laid out the hours by rule, added the lines of seasonal qi, and so made a plane solar gnomon.

sentences.zh: 又今所用員石欹晷是為赤道晷，亦用所得正子午線較定。

translations.literal: The slanted stone gnomon dial we now use is the equatorial dial; it too was checked with the true south-north line we obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The slanted stone dial we now use is the equatorial dial; it too was verified against the true south-north line we obtained.

sentences.zh: 此二晷皆可得天之正時刻，所為晝測日也。

translations.literal: Both dials can yield heaven’s true hours; this is what is meant by measuring the sun by day.
translations.idiomatic: Both dials can yield heaven’s true hours—this is what is meant by measuring the sun by day.

sentences.zh: 若測星之晷，實《周禮》夜考極星之法。

translations.literal: The dial for measuring stars is in fact the method in the Rites of Zhou of examining the pole star by night.
translations.idiomatic: The star-measuring dial is in fact the Rites of Zhou method of examining the pole star by night.

sentences.zh: 然古時北極星正當不動之處，今時久漸移，已去不動處三度有奇，舊法不可復用。

translations.literal: In antiquity the north pole star stood exactly at the unmoving place; over long ages it has gradually shifted and now lies more than three degrees from that place—the old method can no longer be used.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the north pole star stood exactly at the unmoving point; over long ages it has drifted and now lies more than three degrees away—the old method can no longer serve.

sentences.zh: 故用重盤星晷，上書時刻，下書節氣，仰測近極二星即得時刻，所謂夜測星也。

translations.literal: Therefore we use the double-disk star gnomon, with hours marked on the upper disk and seasonal qi on the lower; looking up at the two stars near the pole through it we obtain the hour—this is what is called measuring stars by night.
translations.idiomatic: So we use the double-disk star gnomon: hours on the upper disk, seasonal qi on the lower; gazing up at the two stars near the pole through it we read the hour—this is what is called measuring stars by night.

sentences.zh: 七年，督修曆法右參政李天經言：

translations.literal: Year 7, Right Vice Commissioner Li Tianjing, supervising calendar reform, said:
translations.idiomatic: In year seven Li Tianjing, right vice commissioner supervising calendar reform, said:

sentences.zh: 輔臣光啟言定時之法，古有壺漏，近有輪鐘，二者皆由人力遷就，不如求端於日星，以天合天，乃為本法，特請制日晷、星晷、望遠鏡三器。

translations.literal: Assistant Minister Xu Guangqi spoke of the method of fixing time: antiquity had clepsydra, recent times have wheel-clocks—both are human adjustments and cannot match seeking the origin in sun and stars; to harmonize heaven with heaven is the true method. He specially requested making solar gnomon, star gnomon, and telescope, three instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Minister Xu Guangqi said that in fixing time antiquity had clepsydras and recent times wheel-clocks—both are human makeshifts. Better to seek the origin in sun and stars: heaven matched to heaven is the true method. He therefore asked especially for three instruments—the solar gnomon, star gnomon, and telescope.

sentences.zh: 臣奉命接管，敢先言其略。

translations.literal: Your servant received the charge and ventures first to set out the outline.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant received the charge and ventures first to set out the outline.

sentences.zh: 日晷者，礱石為平面，界節氣十三線，內冬夏二至各一線，其余日行相等之節氣，皆兩節氣同一線也。

translations.literal: As for the solar gnomon: a stone is polished into a plane, bounded by thirteen lines of seasonal qi; within, winter and summer solstices each have one line, while the rest of the equal-moving qi share one line between every two seasons.
translations.idiomatic: As for the solar gnomon: a stone is polished flat and marked with thirteen lines of seasonal qi; within, winter and summer solstice each have a line, while the other equal-moving qi share one line between every two seasons.

sentences.zh: 平面之周列時刻線，以各節氣太陽出入為限。

translations.literal: Around the plane’s rim hour-lines are set, limited by the sun’s rising and setting at each seasonal qi.
translations.idiomatic: Around the plane’s rim hour-lines are drawn, bounded by the sun’s rising and setting at each seasonal qi.

sentences.zh: 又依京師北極出地度，范為三角銅表置其中。

translations.literal: Also according to the capital’s north-pole altitude, a triangular bronze table is cast and set at the center.
translations.idiomatic: According to the capital’s north-pole altitude, a triangular bronze table is cast and set at the center.

sentences.zh: 表體之全影指時刻，表中之銳影指節氣。

translations.literal: The table’s full shadow points to the hour; the sharp shadow within points to the seasonal qi.
translations.idiomatic: The table’s full shadow points to the hour; the sharp inner shadow points to the seasonal qi.

sentences.zh: 此日晷之大略也。

translations.literal: Such is the outline of the solar gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the outline of the solar gnomon.

sentences.zh: 星晷者，治銅為柱，上安重盤。

translations.literal: As for the star gnomon: bronze is worked into a pillar with a double disk mounted above.
translations.idiomatic: As for the star gnomon: bronze is cast into a pillar with a double disk above.

sentences.zh: 內盤鐫周天度數，列十二宮以分節氣，外盤鐫列時刻，中橫刻一縫，用以窺星。

translations.literal: The inner disk is cut with degrees of the whole heaven and the twelve palaces to divide seasonal qi; the outer disk is cut with hours; a horizontal slit is carved through the center for sighting stars.
translations.idiomatic: The inner disk is engraved with degrees of the whole heaven and the twelve palaces to divide seasonal qi; the outer disk with hours; a horizontal slit is cut through the center for sighting stars.

sentences.zh: 法將外盤子正初刻移對內盤節氣，乃轉移銅盤北望帝星與句陳大星，使兩星同見縫中，即視盤面銳表所指，為正時刻。

translations.literal: The method: align the outer disk’s zi initial quarter with the inner disk’s seasonal qi, then turn the bronze disk and look north at the Imperial Star and the great star of Gouchen until both stars appear in the slit together; then read where the sharp pointer on the disk face points—that is the true hour.
translations.idiomatic: The method: set the outer disk’s zi initial quarter against the inner disk’s seasonal qi, then turn the bronze disk and look north at the Imperial Star and the great Gouchen star until both appear together in the slit; wherever the sharp pointer on the disk face points is the true hour.

sentences.zh: 此星晷之大略也。

translations.literal: Such is the outline of the star gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the outline of the star gnomon.

sentences.zh: 若夫望遠鏡，亦名窺筒，其制虛管層疊相套，使可伸縮，兩端俱用玻璃，隨所視物之遠近以為長短。

translations.literal: As for the far-sight tube, also called the peeping tube: its form is hollow tubes stacked and nested so they may extend and contract, glass is used at both ends, and the length is set according to how near or far the object viewed is.
translations.idiomatic: The far-sight tube—also called the peeping tube—consists of hollow tubes nested one inside another so they can slide in and out. Glass caps both ends, and you adjust the length to match the distance of whatever you wish to see.

sentences.zh: 不但可以窺天象，且能攝數裡外物如在目前，可以望敵施砲，有大用焉。

translations.literal: Not only may one peer at celestial phenomena, but it can also draw objects many li away as if they were before the eyes; one may watch the enemy and aim cannon—of great use indeed.
translations.idiomatic: It serves not only to watch the heavens but to pull objects miles away up before your eyes—as if they stood at arm's length—so you can spy on the foe and lay cannon. Its uses are considerable.

sentences.zh: 至於日晷、星晷皆用措置得宜，必須築台，以便安放。

translations.literal: As for sundials and star dials, both require proper placement; a platform must be built for convenient installation.
translations.idiomatic: Sundials and star-dials alike must be set up with care, and a terrace must be built to receive them.

sentences.zh: 帝命太監盧維寧、魏國徵至局驗試用法。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the eunuchs Lu Weining and Wei Guozheng to go to the bureau to verify and test the method of use.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the eunuchs Lu Weining and Wei Guozheng to the bureau to test how the instruments were to be used.

sentences.zh: 明年，天經又請造沙漏。

translations.literal: The next year Tian Jing again requested that a sand clepsydra be made.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Li Tianjing again petitioned for a sand clepsydra to be built.

sentences.zh: 明初，詹希元以水漏至嚴寒水凍輒不能行，故以沙代水。

translations.literal: In early Ming, Zhan Xiyuan, because in severe cold the water of the water clepsydra would freeze and could not run, used sand in place of water.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty Zhan Xiyuan found that in bitter cold the water clepsydra froze and would not run, so he substituted sand for water.

sentences.zh: 然沙行太疾，未協天運，乃以斗輪之外復加四輪，輪皆三十六齒。

translations.literal: Yet the sand ran too swiftly and did not accord with Heaven's motion; therefore beyond the dipper wheel four more wheels were added, each wheel having thirty-six teeth.
translations.idiomatic: But sand flows too fast to keep pace with the sky. He therefore added four wheels beyond the dipper-wheel, each cut with thirty-six teeth.

sentences.zh: 厥後周述學病其竅太小，而沙易堙，乃更制為六輪，其五輪悉三十齒，而微裕其竅，運行始與晷協。

translations.literal: Later Zhou Shuxue, finding the orifices too small and the sand easily clogged, remade it with six wheels; the five wheels all had thirty teeth, and the orifices were slightly enlarged—only then did its running accord with the sundial.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou Shuxue judged the holes too fine and the sand too prone to clogging. He rebuilt the device with six wheels—the five outer wheels each bore thirty teeth—and widened the holes slightly. Only then did its pace match the gnomon.

sentences.zh: 天經所請，殆其遺意歟。

translations.literal: What Tian Jing requested was probably in the spirit of this legacy.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjing's request was very likely meant to follow this earlier design.

sentences.zh: 夫制器尚象，乃天文家之首務。

translations.literal: To make instruments that mirror the heavens is the astronomer's foremost task.
translations.idiomatic: Fashioning instruments that embody the heavens is the first duty of anyone who studies the sky.

sentences.zh: 然精其術者可以因心而作。

translations.literal: Yet those who master the art may create according to the mind's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who truly master the art can invent according to the mind's own design.

sentences.zh: 故西洋人測天之器，其名未易悉數，內渾蓋、簡平二儀其最精者也。

translations.literal: The Westerners' instruments for measuring Heaven—their names are not easily all enumerated; of these the armillary sphere and the simplified plane instrument are the most refined.
translations.idiomatic: The Westerners' celestial instruments are too many to list in full; among them the armillary sphere and the simplified plane instrument are the finest.

sentences.zh: 其說具見全書，茲不載。

translations.literal: Their explanations are set out fully in the complete book; they are not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Their theory is given at length in the full treatise and is not repeated here.

sentences.zh: ▲極度晷影 宣城梅文鼎曰：

translations.literal: ▲ Pole altitude and gnomon shadow. Mei Wending of Xuancheng says:
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Pole altitude and gnomon shadow. Mei Wending of Xuancheng writes:

sentences.zh: 極度晷影常相因。

translations.literal: Pole altitude and gnomon shadow are constantly interdependent.
translations.idiomatic: Pole altitude and gnomon shadow always depend on one another.

sentences.zh: 知北極出地之高，即可知各節氣午正之影。

translations.literal: Know the height at which the north pole rises above the ground, and you may know the noon shadow at each solar term.
translations.idiomatic: Know how high the north pole stands above the horizon, and you can derive the noon shadow for every solar term.

sentences.zh: 測得各節氣午正之影，亦可知北極之高。

translations.literal: Measure the noon shadow at each solar term, and you may also know the height of the north pole.
translations.idiomatic: Measure those noon shadows, and you can work back to the pole's height.

sentences.zh: 然其術非易易也。

translations.literal: Yet the technique is not easily mastered.
translations.idiomatic: The method itself, however, is far from easy.

sentences.zh: 圭表之法，表短則分秒難明，表長則影虛而淡。

translations.literal: In the gnomon-table method, if the gnomon is short, minutes and seconds are hard to discern; if the gnomon is long, the shadow is faint and diffuse.
translations.idiomatic: With the gnomon table, a short post makes minutes and seconds hard to read; a tall post yields a shadow so faint and diffuse that precision fails.

sentences.zh: 郭守敬所以立四丈之表，用影符以取之也。

translations.literal: This is why Guo Shoujing erected a table forty chi high and used a shadow marker to take the reading.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Guo Shoujing raised a gnomon forty chi tall and took his readings with a shadow marker.

sentences.zh: 日體甚大，豎表所測者日體上邊之影，橫表所測者日體下邊之影，皆非中心之數，郭守敬所以於表端架橫梁以測之也，其術可謂善矣。

translations.literal: The sun's body is very large; what a vertical gnomon measures is the shadow of the sun's upper edge, and what a horizontal gnomon measures is the shadow of the lower edge—neither is the central number. This is why Guo Shoujing set a crossbeam atop the gnomon to measure it; the technique may be called excellent.
translations.idiomatic: The sun is a vast disk. A vertical gnomon catches the shadow of its upper rim; a horizontal one catches the lower rim—neither gives the sun's center. Guo Shoujing therefore bridged the top of the gnomon with a crossbeam for the measurement. The method is as clever as it is sound.

sentences.zh: 但其影符之制，用銅片鑽針芥之孔，雖前低後仰以向太陽，但太陽之高低每日不同，銅片之欹側安能俱合。

translations.literal: Yet in the making of the shadow marker he drilled a hole the size of a mustard seed in a copper sheet; though the sheet was tilted low in front and high behind to face the sun, the sun's altitude differs every day—how could the sheet's slant always match?
translations.idiomatic: His shadow marker, however, was a copper plate pierced with a hole no larger than a mustard seed. Though the plate was pitched to face the sun, the sun's height changes daily; the plate's angle cannot follow every shift.

sentences.zh: 不合則光不透，臨時遷就，而日已西移矣。

translations.literal: When it does not match, light does not pass through; one adjusts on the spot, and already the sun has moved west.
translations.idiomatic: When the angle is wrong, no light passes through; you adjust by hand—and the sun has already slipped westward.

sentences.zh: 須易銅片以圓木，左右用兩板架之，如車軸然，則轉動甚易。

translations.literal: One must replace the copper sheet with a round wooden rod, with a board on either side to support it like an axle—then rotation is very easy.
translations.idiomatic: Replace the copper with a round wooden cylinder, braced on either side by boards like an axle, and it turns with ease.

sentences.zh: 更易圓孔以直縫，而用始便也。

translations.literal: Change the round hole further into a straight slit, and use becomes convenient at once.
translations.idiomatic: Trade the round aperture for a straight slit, and the device is far easier to use.

sentences.zh: 然影符止可去虛淡之弊，而非其本。

translations.literal: Yet the shadow marker can only remove the flaw of faintness and diffusion; it is not the root of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, the shadow marker only remedies faint, diffuse shadows—it does not touch the root of the problem.

sentences.zh: 必須正其表焉，平其圭焉，均其度焉，三者缺一，不可以得影。

translations.literal: The gnomon must be made true, the table plane leveled, and the graduations even; if any one of these three is lacking, the shadow cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The gnomon must stand true, the table must lie level, and the graduations must be even. Fail in any one of these three, and no trustworthy shadow can be had.

sentences.zh: 三者得矣，而人心有粗細，目力有利鈍，任事有誠偽，不可不擇也。

translations.literal: When the three are obtained, yet the human mind has coarse and fine degrees, the eye sharp and dull, and those who take the work sincere or false—one cannot but choose carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Even when all three are right, minds differ in fineness, eyes in keenness, and workers in honesty. The observer must be chosen with care.

sentences.zh: 知乎此，庶幾晷影可得矣。

translations.literal: Know this, and then perhaps the gnomon shadow may be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Only with this understood may one hope to read the gnomon shadow aright.

sentences.zh: 西洋之法又有進焉。

translations.literal: The Western method goes still further.
translations.idiomatic: Western methods go further still.

sentences.zh: 謂地半徑居日天半徑千餘分之一，則地面所測太陽之高，必少於地心之實高，於是有地半徑差之加。

translations.literal: They say that because the earth's radius is about one part in more than a thousand of the sun's celestial radius, the sun's altitude measured from the ground must be less than the true altitude from the earth's center; hence there is an addition for the earth-radius difference.
translations.idiomatic: They hold that because the earth's radius is scarcely more than one part in a thousand of the sun's celestial radius, the sun's altitude measured from the ground is always lower than the true altitude from the earth's center. A correction for the earth's radius must therefore be added.

sentences.zh: 近地有清蒙氣，能升卑為高，則晷影所推太陽之高，或多於天上之實高，於是又有清蒙差之減。

translations.literal: Near the earth there is clear, hazy air that can raise what is low to seem high; thus the sun's altitude inferred from the gnomon shadow may be greater than the true altitude in the heavens—hence there is also a subtraction for the clear-haze difference.
translations.idiomatic: Near the surface, clear haze lifts low things so they appear higher. The sun's altitude inferred from the gnomon shadow may therefore exceed its true height in the sky. A correction for this clear haze must be subtracted.

sentences.zh: 是二差者，皆近地多而漸高漸減，以至於無，地半徑差至天頂而無，清蒙差至四十五度而無也。

translations.literal: Both differences are greater near the ground and, rising higher, gradually diminish until they vanish; the earth-radius difference vanishes at the zenith, and the clear-haze difference vanishes at forty-five degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Both corrections are largest near the ground and taper away with altitude until they disappear entirely—the earth-radius correction at the zenith, the haze correction at forty-five degrees.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，西洋人測得京省北極出地度分：北京四十度，周天三百六十度，度六十分立算，下同。

translations.literal: In early Chongzhen the Westerners measured the degrees and minutes of the north pole's altitude above the ground for the provinces and capital: Beijing forty degrees. The full circle is three hundred sixty degrees, with sixty minutes per degree in calculation; the same applies below.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign Western astronomers measured how far the north pole stood above the horizon for the capital and provinces: Beijing, forty degrees. The full circle is three hundred sixty degrees, each degree divided into sixty minutes in calculation—the same rule holds throughout what follows.

sentences.zh: 南京三十二度半，山東三十七度，山西三十八度，陝西三十六度，河南三十五度，浙江三十度，江西二十九度，湖廣三十一度，四川二十九度，廣東二十三度，福建二十六度，廣西二十五度，雲南二十二度，貴州二十四度。

translations.literal: Nanjing thirty-two and a half degrees, Shandong thirty-seven, Shanxi thirty-eight, Shaanxi thirty-six, Henan thirty-five, Zhejiang thirty, Jiangxi twenty-nine, Huguang thirty-one, Sichuan twenty-nine, Guangdong twenty-three, Fujian twenty-six, Guangxi twenty-five, Yunnan twenty-two, Guizhou twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing, thirty-two and a half degrees; Shandong, thirty-seven; Shanxi, thirty-eight; Shaanxi, thirty-six; Henan, thirty-five; Zhejiang, thirty; Jiangxi, twenty-nine; Huguang, thirty-one; Sichuan, twenty-nine; Guangdong, twenty-three; Fujian, twenty-six; Guangxi, twenty-five; Yunnan, twenty-two; Guizhou, twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 以上極度，惟兩京、江西、廣東四處皆系實測，其余則據地圖約計之。

translations.literal: Of the pole altitudes above, only the two capitals, Jiangxi, and Guangdong were obtained by actual measurement; the rest were roughly estimated from maps.
translations.idiomatic: Of these pole altitudes, only the two capitals, Jiangxi, and Guangdong were measured on site; the remainder were approximated from maps.

sentences.zh: 又以十二度度六十分之表測京師各節氣午正日影：夏至三度三十三分，芒種、小暑三度四十二分，小滿、大暑四度十五分，立夏、立秋五度六分，谷雨、處暑六度二十三分，清明、白露八度六分，春、秋分十度四分，驚蟄、寒露十二度二十六分，雨水、霜降十五度五分，立春、立冬十七度四十七分，大寒、小雪二十度四十七分，小寒、大雪二十三度三十分，冬至二十四度四分。

translations.literal: With a gnomon of twelve degrees and sixty minutes they measured the noon sun-shadow at Beijing for each solar term: summer solstice three degrees thirty-three minutes; Grain in Beard and Lesser Heat three degrees forty-two minutes; Lesser Fullness and Greater Heat four degrees fifteen minutes; Beginning of Summer and Beginning of Autumn five degrees six minutes; Grain Rain and End of Heat six degrees twenty-three minutes; Clear Bright and White Dew eight degrees six minutes; spring and autumn equinoxes ten degrees four minutes; Waking of Insects and Cold Dew twelve degrees twenty-six minutes; Rain Water and Frost's Descent fifteen degrees five minutes; Beginning of Spring and Beginning of Winter seventeen degrees forty-seven minutes; Greater Cold and Lesser Snow twenty degrees forty-seven minutes; Lesser Cold and Greater Snow twenty-three degrees thirty minutes; winter solstice twenty-four degrees four minutes.
translations.idiomatic: With a gnomon scaled at twelve degrees and sixty minutes they measured Beijing's noon shadows through the year: at the summer solstice, three degrees thirty-three minutes; at Grain in Beard and Lesser Heat, three degrees forty-two; at Lesser Fullness and Greater Heat, four degrees fifteen; at Beginning of Summer and Beginning of Autumn, five degrees six; at Grain Rain and End of Heat, six degrees twenty-three; at Clear Bright and White Dew, eight degrees six; at the equinoxes, ten degrees four; at Waking of Insects and Cold Dew, twelve degrees twenty-six; at Rain Water and Frost's Descent, fifteen degrees five; at Beginning of Spring and Beginning of Winter, seventeen degrees forty-seven; at Greater Cold and Lesser Snow, twenty degrees forty-seven; at Lesser Cold and Greater Snow, twenty-three degrees thirty; at the winter solstice, twenty-four degrees four.

sentences.zh: ▲東西偏度 以京師子午線為中，而較各地所偏之度。

translations.literal: ▲ East-west offset in degrees. Taking the Beijing meridian as center, one compares the degrees by which each place is offset.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ East-west offset in degrees. With Beijing's meridian as the standard, one compares how far each region lies to east or west.

sentences.zh: 凡節氣之早晚，月食之先後，胥視此。

translations.literal: Whether solar terms come early or late, or lunar eclipses come sooner or later—all depend on this.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the solar terms arrive early or late, or an eclipse is seen sooner or later, all hinge on this.

sentences.zh: 蓋人各以見日出入為東西為卯酉，以日中為南為午。

translations.literal: Each person takes the sun's rising and setting as east and west, mao and you, and noon as south and the wu hour.
translations.idiomatic: Every observer takes sunrise and sunset for east and west—the mao and you hours—and midday for south and the wu hour.

sentences.zh: 而東方見日早，西方見日遲。

translations.literal: Yet the east sees the sun early and the west sees it late.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the east sees the sun before the west does.

sentences.zh: 東西相距三十度則差一時。

translations.literal: Where east and west are thirty degrees apart, the time differs by one double-hour.
translations.idiomatic: Where east and west are separated by thirty degrees, local time differs by one double-hour.

sentences.zh: 東方之午乃西方之巳，西方之午乃東方之未也。

translations.literal: Noon in the east is the si hour in the west; noon in the west is the wei hour in the east.
translations.idiomatic: When it is noon in the east, it is already si in the west; when it is noon in the west, it is still wei in the east.

sentences.zh: 相距九十度則差三時。

translations.literal: Where they are ninety degrees apart, the difference is three double-hours.
translations.idiomatic: At ninety degrees' separation the difference is three double-hours.

sentences.zh: 東方之午乃西方之卯，西方之午乃東方之酉也。

translations.literal: Noon in the east is the mao hour in the west; noon in the west is the you hour in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Noon in the east corresponds to mao in the west; noon in the west to you in the east.

sentences.zh: 相距一百八十度則晝夜時刻俱反對矣。

translations.literal: Where they are one hundred eighty degrees apart, day and night and the hours are wholly opposed.
translations.idiomatic: At one hundred eighty degrees, day and night—and every hour—stand directly opposed.

sentences.zh: 東方之午乃西方之子。

translations.literal: Noon in the east is the zi hour in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Noon in the east is midnight—zi—in the west.

sentences.zh: 西洋人湯若望曰「天啟三年九月十五夜，戌初初刻望，月食，京師初虧在酉初一刻十二分，而西洋意大裡雅諸國望在晝，不見。

translations.literal: The Westerner Adam Schall said: "On the night of the fifteenth day of the ninth month of the third year of Tianqi, at the beginning of the xu watch, full moon—a lunar eclipse. At the capital the first contact was at the beginning of the you hour, one ke and twelve fen; in the Western lands of Italy and the like the full moon fell in daylight and was not seen.
translations.idiomatic: The Westerner Adam Schall wrote: "On the night of the fifteenth of the ninth month in the third year of Tianqi, at the opening of the xu watch, the moon was full and suffered eclipse. At the capital first contact came at the start of you, one ke and twelve fen; in Italy and the other Western realms the moon was full by day and the eclipse went unseen.

sentences.zh: 推其初虧在巳正三刻四分，相差三時二刻八分，以裡差計之，殆距京師之西九十九度半也。

translations.literal: Calculating back, their first contact was at the exact si hour, three ke and four fen—a difference of three double-hours, two ke, and eight fen. Computing by longitudinal difference, that land lies roughly ninety-nine and a half degrees west of the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Working backward, their first contact would have been at exact si, three ke and four fen—three double-hours, two ke, and eight fen earlier than Beijing. By the longitudinal correction, that country lies about ninety-nine and a half degrees west of the capital."

sentences.zh: 故欲定東西偏度，必須兩地同測一月食，較其時刻。

translations.literal: Therefore to fix the east-west offset in degrees, two places must observe the same lunar eclipse and compare the times.
translations.idiomatic: To fix the east-west offset, two places must observe the same lunar eclipse and compare their times.

sentences.zh: 若早六十分時之二則為偏西一度，遲六十分時之二則為偏東一度。

translations.literal: If one place is early by two parts in sixty parts of a double-hour, it is one degree west; if late by two parts in sixty, it is one degree east.
translations.idiomatic: If one site is early by two sixtieths of a double-hour, it lies one degree to the west; if late by two sixtieths, one degree to the east.

sentences.zh: 節氣之遲早亦同。

translations.literal: The earliness or lateness of the solar terms follows the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: The earliness or lateness of the solar terms follows the same rule.

sentences.zh: 今各省差數未得測驗，據廣輿圖計裡之方約略條列，或不致甚舛也。

translations.literal: Today the offset numbers for each province have not been obtained by measurement; relying on the broad map to estimate li by the square, they are roughly listed below, so that gross error may be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: The offsets for the provinces have not yet been measured on the ground. The figures below are roughly estimated from the broad map by squaring distances in li, and are given so that gross error may be avoided.

sentences.zh: 南京應天府、福建福州府並偏東一度，山東濟南府偏東一度十五分，山西太原府偏西六度，湖廣武昌府、河南開封府偏西三度四十五分，陝西西安府、廣西桂林府偏西八度半，浙江杭州府偏東三度，江西南昌府偏西二度半，廣東廣州府偏西五度，四川成都府偏四十三度，貴州貴陽府偏西九度半，雲南雲南府偏西十七度。」

translations.literal: Nanjing Prefecture of Yingtian and Fuzhou Prefecture of Fujian are each one degree east; Jinan Prefecture of Shandong one degree fifteen fen east; Taiyuan Prefecture of Shanxi six degrees west; Wuchang Prefecture of Huguang and Kaifeng Prefecture of Henan three degrees forty-five fen west; Xi'an Prefecture of Shaanxi and Guilin Prefecture of Guangxi eight and a half degrees west; Hangzhou Prefecture of Zhejiang three degrees east; Nanchang Prefecture of Jiangxi two and a half degrees west; Guangzhou Prefecture of Guangdong five degrees west; Chengdu Prefecture of Sichuan forty-three degrees west; Guiyang Prefecture of Guizhou nine and a half degrees west; Yunnan Prefecture of Yunnan seventeen degrees west."
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing in Yingtian and Fuzhou in Fujian each lie one degree east; Jinan in Shandong, one degree fifteen fen east; Taiyuan in Shanxi, six degrees west; Wuchang in Huguang and Kaifeng in Henan, three degrees forty-five fen west; Xi'an in Shaanxi and Guilin in Guangxi, eight and a half degrees west; Hangzhou in Zhejiang, three degrees east; Nanchang in Jiangxi, two and a half degrees west; Guangzhou in Guangdong, five degrees west; Chengdu in Sichuan, forty-three degrees west; Guiyang in Guizhou, nine and a half degrees west; Yunnan in Yunnan, seventeen degrees west."

sentences.zh: 右偏度，載《崇禎歷書》交食歷指。

translations.literal: The offsets above are recorded in the Eclipse Treatise of the Chongzhen Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: These offsets are recorded in the Eclipse Treatise of the Chongzhen Calendar.

sentences.zh: 其時開局修歷，未暇分測，度數實多未確，存之以備考訂雲。

translations.literal: At that time the calendar bureau was opened to revise the calendar, and there was no leisure to measure each place separately; many of the degrees were in fact not yet exact, and they are kept here for later correction.
translations.idiomatic: When the calendar office was first opened to revise the almanac, there was no time to survey each region separately; many of the figures were still uncertain. They are preserved here for later revision.

sentences.zh: ▲中星 古今中星不同，由於歲差。

translations.literal: ▲ Culminating stars at dusk and dawn. The culminating stars at dusk and dawn differ between antiquity and the present because of precession.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Culminating stars at dusk and dawn. The stars culminating at dusk and dawn differ between antiquity and today because of precession.

sentences.zh: 而歲差之說，中西復異。

translations.literal: Yet the doctrine of precession also differs between China and the West.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese and Western accounts of precession, however, do not agree.

sentences.zh: 中法謂節氣差而西，西法謂恆星差而東，然其歸一也。

translations.literal: The Chinese method holds that the solar terms drift westward; the Western method holds that the fixed stars drift eastward—yet in the end they come to one.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese theory says the solar terms slip westward; Western theory says the fixed stars slip eastward—yet both describe the same motion.

sentences.zh: 今將李天經、湯若望等所推崇禎元年京師昏旦時刻中星列於後。

translations.literal: Now the times of dusk and dawn and the culminating stars at Beijing in the first year of Chongzhen, as promoted by Li Tianjing, Adam Schall, and others, are listed below.
translations.idiomatic: Below are the dusk and dawn times and culminating stars for Beijing in the first Chongzhen year, as calculated by Li Tianjing, Adam Schall, and their colleagues.

sentences.zh: 春分，戌初二刻五分昏，北河三中；

translations.literal: Spring equinox: at dusk, five fen past the second ke of early xu, the third star of Beihe at culmination;
translations.idiomatic: Spring equinox—dusk at five fen past the second ke of early xu, with the third star of Beihe on the meridian;

sentences.zh: 寅正一刻一十分旦，尾中。

translations.literal: at dawn, ten fen past the first ke of exact yin, Wei at culmination.
translations.idiomatic: dawn at ten fen past the first ke of exact yin, with Wei on the meridian.

sentences.zh: 清明，戌初三刻十三分昏，七星偏東四度；

translations.literal: Clear Bright: at dusk, thirteen fen past the third ke of xu, the Seven Stars four degrees east of culmination;
translations.idiomatic: Clear Bright—dusk at thirteen fen past the third ke of xu, the Seven Stars four degrees east of the meridian;

sentences.zh: 昏旦時或無正中之星，則取中前、中後之大星用之。

translations.literal: When at dusk or dawn there is no star exactly at culmination, take a major star just before or just after culmination.
translations.idiomatic: when no star stands exactly on the meridian at dusk or dawn, use a bright star slightly before or after culmination.

sentences.zh: 距中三度以內者，為時不及一刻，可勿論。

translations.literal: Within three degrees of culmination the time falls short of one ke and may be disregarded.
translations.idiomatic: Within three degrees of the meridian the time error is less than one ke and may be ignored.

sentences.zh: 四度以上，去中稍遠，故紀其偏度焉。

translations.literal: Beyond four degrees, farther from culmination, the offset in degrees is therefore recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond four degrees, farther from the meridian, the offset is recorded in degrees.

sentences.zh: 寅正初刻二分旦，帝座中。

translations.literal: at dawn, two fen past the first ke of exact yin, Emperor's Seat at culmination.
translations.idiomatic: dawn at two fen past the first ke of exact yin, Emperor's Seat on the meridian.

sentences.zh: 谷雨，戌正一刻七分昏，翼偏東七度；

translations.literal: Grain Rain: at dusk, seven fen past the first ke of exact xu, Wings seven degrees east of culmination;
translations.idiomatic: Grain Rain—dusk at seven fen past the first ke of exact xu, Wings seven degrees east of the meridian;

sentences.zh: 寅初二刻八分旦，箕偏東四度。

translations.literal: at dawn, eight fen past the second ke of early yin, Winnowing Basket four degrees east of culmination.
translations.idiomatic: dawn at eight fen past the second ke of early yin, Winnowing Basket four degrees east of the meridian.

sentences.zh: 立夏，戌正三刻二分昏，軫偏東五度；

translations.literal: Beginning of Summer: at dusk, two fen past the third ke of exact xu, Chariot Shaft five degrees east of culmination;
translations.idiomatic: Beginning of Summer—dusk at two fen past the third ke of exact xu, Chariot Shaft five degrees east of the meridian;

sentences.zh: 寅初初刻十三分旦，箕偏西四度。

translations.literal: at dawn, thirteen fen past the first ke of early yin, Winnowing Basket four degrees west of culmination.
translations.idiomatic: dawn at thirteen fen past the first ke of early yin, Winnowing Basket four degrees west of the meridian.

sentences.zh: 小滿，亥初初刻十二分昏，角中；

translations.literal: Lesser Fullness: at dusk, twelve fen past the first ke of early hai, Horn at culmination;
translations.idiomatic: Lesser Fullness—dusk at twelve fen past the first ke of early hai, Horn on the meridian;

sentences.zh: 醜正三刻三分旦，箕中。

translations.literal: at dawn, three fen past the third ke of exact chou, Winnowing Basket at culmination.
translations.idiomatic: dawn at three fen past the third ke of exact chou, Winnowing Basket on the meridian.

sentences.zh: 芒種，亥初一刻十二分昏，大角偏西六度；

translations.literal: Grain in Beard: at dusk, twelve fen past the first ke of hai, Great Horn six degrees west of culmination;
translations.idiomatic: Grain in Beard—dusk at twelve fen past the first ke of hai, Great Horn six degrees west of the meridian;

sentences.zh: 醜正二刻三分旦，河鼓二中。

translations.literal: at dawn, three fen past the second ke of exact chou, the second star of River Drum at culmination.
translations.idiomatic: dawn at three fen past the second ke of exact chou, the second star of River Drum on the meridian.

sentences.zh: 夏至，亥初二刻五分昏，房中；

translations.literal: Summer solstice: at dusk, five fen past the second ke of early hai, Room at culmination;

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era of Tang, Li Chunfeng compiled the Treatise on Astro-omen Patterns, using the twelve celestial degrees of the Book of Han to pair with Tang prefectures and counties; Yi Xing held that the image of mountains and rivers under Heaven resides between the two northern and southern boundaries—his discussion is exhaustive.

Yi Xing argued that the pattern of the realm’s mountains and rivers is held between a northern and a southern limit—his account is far more detailed.

sentences.zh: 洪武十七年，《大明清類天文分野書》成，頒賜秦、晉二王。

sentences.zh: 其書大略謂「《晉天文志》分野始角、亢者，以東方蒼龍為首也。

translations.literal: In antiquity all who spoke of Heaven started from Dipper and Ox to mark the stars, hence the name Xingji—this is the reason for the choice.’
